newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower, ignores Dunavant forecast.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower, ignores Dunavant forecast.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled slightly lower despite a bullish speech by closely-watched cotton merchant William Dunavant.
In a speech to industry members at a foreign policy conference in Memphis, Dunavant raised his estimate for exports in 1996/97 to 6.8 million bales from a previous forecast of 6.4 million bales.
Indeed, floor sources cited market talk of large sales to China and Brazil that could appear in Thursday's U.S. Department of Agriculture export and sales report.

Dunavant also raised his estimate for domestic consumption to 11.0 million bales from 10.9 million bales, for the current crop year. He also raised his planted area forecast to 14.2 million from 13.8 million acres.
Traders said the speech probably did not filter into the market and could lift prices Wednesday. Producer selling kept the market under pressure, they said.
Resistance was seen at the day's high of 75.50 cents in March, and support at 73.00 cents.
The March contract ended down 0.15 at 75.11, traded 75.50 to 74.90. The back months settled 0.08 lower to 0.45 higher.
